summary: What happens to a deposit after it has been taken: the formula that set it, the ways a deal ends, the money going back, and the three things Hamzist will arbitrate. The payment service is renamed ANIMAL_SALE_DEPOSIT, and the migration renames the enum value rather than dropping and recreating the type as the generator proposed — recreating it would fail the cast on any payment already recorded, and a migration must not destroy a verified payment's own record of what it paid for. PRODUCT_DECISIONS §5 makes the commission a fixed amount plus a percentage 'by animal kind and seller kind', which a single pair of global settings cannot express, so the formula became published immutable rows: one live rule per species, optionally narrowed to a seller kind, resolved most-specific-first and falling back to the global settings of PROMPT-002 and then to NOT_CONFIGURED. Publishing archives the previous rule in the same transaction, so there is never a moment with two live formulas or none, and a deal freezes the id of the rule it was priced by alongside the figures that rule produced. The cancellation policy is frozen the same way, at acceptance: the buyer penalty in basis points, the seller penalty and the restriction period are written onto the deal, so a penalty edited tomorrow cannot reach into a deal struck today. An unset penalty stays null all the way to the outcome, where it means no penalty was agreed — never a zero somebody could later mistake for a decision, and never a fee invented at the moment somebody cancels. A buyer who changes their mind pays the frozen penalty, truncated and capped at the deposit. A seller who cancels returns the whole deposit — nothing is deducted from money that is not theirs — and owes the penalty as a separate debt, with a publisher restriction whose period multiplies with each previous cancellation and which reuses the restriction mechanism that already exists. The five reasons that are claims about the animal, the advert or a meeting nobody attended produce AWAITING_REVIEW and a dispute instead of a refund: the animal stays reserved while the argument is open, because releasing it would sell it out from under the case. A refund is a record with a life of its own — pending, attempted, failed, retried — and every attempt leaves a row naming the provider, its idempotency key and what it said. PAID is impossible without a provider or bank reference, enforced by a check constraint as well as by the code; a gateway with no automated refund here produces MANUAL_REQUIRED, which is the truth rather than a silence; three automatic attempts is the limit, after which a person takes it rather than a loop; and the record is claimed under a version guard, so two operators pressing retry together produce one attempt, not two transfers. Arbitration covers the deposit, the truth of the recorded listing facts, and whether the handover happened. Anything about the price settled outside is refused before a row exists, in the same words printed on the reviewer's own page. A decision carries a reason, is written once under a version guard, may return part of the deposit but never more than was paid, and writes the refund it implies inside the same transaction — while sending that money stays a separate, retryable step. Dispute evidence is private storage read through a record-scoped grant: the two parties and the reviewer of that one case, never a whole role across every case.

limitations: No real payment provider refunds anything yet. The gateway contract now has an optional refund method that the development and mock gateways implement; a provider without one produces MANUAL_REQUIRED, and closing that needs a finance operator and a bank reference. Nothing here has been exercised against a live provider, and the report does not claim otherwise.

Refunds are executed by an operator pressing retry, not by a worker. There is no scheduler in this repository, so a failed refund waits in the queue until somebody acts; the queue exists precisely so that waiting is visible rather than silent.

The seller debt book is deliberately small: it records what is owed and who decided it, and cannot move money between accounts. Collecting it, offsetting it against payouts and the multi-vendor ledger belong to PROMPT-011.

A cancellation before the seller accepts needs no code, and none was written: a deposit cannot exist at that point, so PRODUCT_DECISIONS §6's 'full refund before acceptance' is the withdrawal path of PROMPT-005 with nothing to return. That is stated in the service and pinned by a test rather than implemented as dead branches.

Partial refunds exist as one record for the part owed, not as several partial transfers against one deposit. A provider that pays part of a refund and fails on the rest would be recorded as a failed attempt and retried in full; splitting one refund across several transfers is not modelled.

The handover itself — the one-time code, the two-sided confirmation, the transfer of ownership — is PROMPT-007. A dispute here can find that the handover did not happen; it cannot yet be answered from a handover record, because there is none.
